title: On Raising the glass to the oldest guest
subtitle: 经济消费 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）
meta: 主题语境：经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）　|　核心词汇：raise　|　正文 360 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 raise 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 the teacher ① raised the glass to the oldest guest with great care, and every pupil in the classroom said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three terms on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the teacher ② raises the glass to the oldest guest on the same day without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ raise the glass to the oldest guest at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ raised the glass to the oldest guest before — a line in the notebook for March 1960 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Raising the glass to the oldest guest with great care, the teacher said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the ruler at the far blackboard, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ raise the charge for every load on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Raise the charge for every load at once and never mention it again.

By 1973 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the notebook, and a new pupil from the next classroom ⑧ raises the charge for every load with great care every term without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the blackboard, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ raised the glass to the oldest guest again when nobody else would.

⑩ To raise the glass to the oldest guest, my mother said in 1978, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the classroom remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the classroom forgets, somebody raises the glass to the oldest guest on the same day again and somebody must raise the glass to the oldest guest with great care all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 举起（一般过去式 raised the glass to the oldest guest：1966 年先生头一回这样做，小心翼翼地）
B. v. 举起（一般现在 raises the glass to the oldest guest：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 举起（不定式 to raise the glass to the oldest guest：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 举起（过去完成时 had raised the glass to the oldest guest：1960 年三月的笔记簿上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 举起（动名词 raising the glass to the oldest guest 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 抬高（raise the charge for every load：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去抬高把每一趟的运费都抬高）
G. v. 抬高（raise the charge for every load：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 举起（后段两处：新来的学童照例 raises the charge for every load，而母亲又一次 raised the glass to the oldest guest）

answers.why: raise 意为“举起”，1966 年先生小心翼翼地举起向最年长的客人举杯，那是教室里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 raised。
raise 意为“举起”，自那以后先生当天就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 raises。
raise 意为“举起”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯举起向最年长的客人举杯”，此处为不定式 to raise the glass to the oldest guest。
raise 意为“举起”，笔记簿里 三月 那行字说明早在 1973 年之前就有人举起过，故用过去完成时 had raised。
raise 意为“举起”，先生说“举起向最年长的客人举杯这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 raising the glass to the oldest guest 作主语。
raise 意为“抬高”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去抬高把每一趟的运费都抬高”，should ever 之后用原形 raise the charge for every load。
raise 意为“抬高”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻抬高把每一趟的运费都抬高（raise the charge for every load at once），以后再也不要提起。
raise 意为“举起”，新来的学童每个学期都照例抬高把每一趟的运费都抬高，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 raises。
raise 意为“举起”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次小心翼翼地举起向最年长的客人举杯，用一般过去式 raised 叙述。
raise 意为“举起”，结尾那句是母亲 1978 年的话：要举起向最年长的客人举杯，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和教室记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 raise 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1966 the teacher raised the glass to the oldest guest with great care, and nobody in the classroom forgot it.
Even now the teacher raises the glass to the oldest guest on the same day whenever the classroom asks.
Raising the glass to the oldest guest with great care, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever raise the charge for every load on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new pupil from the next classroom raises the charge for every load with great care every term, asking nothing about the past.
